cloze.en: Can you come over for a moment now?

words.notes: 'jetzt' = at this moment. 'nun' is the slightly more written/formal twin.
words.mnemonic: JETZT sounds like 'jet' - a jet takes off right NOW.

example_sentences.en: What are you doing this evening?

cloze.en: Unfortunately I don't have time today.

words.notes: Combine it: 'heute Morgen' = this morning, 'heute Abend' = this evening, 'heute Nacht' = tonight.

example_sentences.en: Yesterday I was at the cinema.

cloze.en: Did you speak with him yesterday?

words.notes: 'vorgestern' = the day before yesterday. 'gestern' almost always goes with the Perfekt in speech.

cloze.en: We're meeting tomorrow at ten.

words.notes: Lowercase 'morgen' = tomorrow; capitalised 'der Morgen' = the morning. 'morgen früh' = tomorrow morning.

example_sentences.de: Ich stehe jeden Tag früh auf.
example_sentences.en: I get up early every day.

cloze.en: Tomorrow I have to get up early.

words.notes: 'früher' also means 'in the past / back in the day', not only 'earlier'.
words.germany_context: German working days start early - many offices are full by 8:00 and Bäckereien open around 6:00.

example_sentences.en: The bus is coming late today.

cloze.en: Sorry, I'm late.

words.notes: 'zu spät sein' = to be late. 'später' = later.
words.germany_context: Lateness is taken seriously: for a Termin or an invitation, more than 5 minutes late needs a short message or an apology.

cloze.en: We'll be there soon.

words.notes: 'Bis bald!' is a normal friendly goodbye when you have no fixed next date.

example_sentences.en: He is on the phone right now.

cloze.en: What are you doing right now?

words.notes: Spoken German often shortens it to 'grade'. As an adjective 'gerade' means 'straight' or 'even (number)'.

cloze.de: Wie lange wohnst du ___ in Berlin?
cloze.en: How long have you been living in Berlin?

words.notes: 'schon' also reassures: 'Das wird schon klappen' = 'It'll work out, don't worry'.

example_sentences.de: Ich wohne noch bei meinen Eltern.
example_sentences.en: I still live with my parents.

cloze.en: Are you still at the office?

words.notes: 'noch nicht' = not yet, 'noch ein' = one more, 'noch nie' = never so far.

example_sentences.de: Ich trinke immer Kaffee am Morgen.
example_sentences.en: I always drink coffee in the morning.

cloze.en: She always helps me.

words.notes: 'immer noch' = still (emphatic), 'immer wieder' = again and again.

example_sentences.de: Wie oft gehst du ins Fitnessstudio?
example_sentences.en: How often do you go to the gym?

cloze.en: We don't see each other often.

words.notes: Comparative: 'öfter' (more often). 'häufig' is the more formal synonym.

example_sentences.de: Manchmal fahre ich mit dem Rad zur Arbeit.
example_sentences.en: Sometimes I ride my bike to work.

cloze.en: Sometimes I don't understand my neighbours.

example_sentences.en: I rarely go to the cinema.

cloze.en: On Sundays the buses run only rarely.

words.notes: Also an adjective: 'ein seltener Fall' = a rare case.
words.germany_context: Sunday timetables for buses and trams are much thinner than weekdays - always check the 'Sonn- und Feiertag' column.

cloze.en: I have never been to Munich.

words.notes: 'niemals' is the emphatic form. 'noch nie' = never up to now.

cloze.en: The lift is broken again.

words.notes: 'wieder' (again) with ie; 'wider' (against) is a different word.

cloze.de: Nach drei Monaten habe ich ___ einen Termin.
cloze.en: After three months I finally have an appointment.

words.notes: Expresses relief after a long wait - not the same as 'schließlich' (in the end).
words.germany_context: Waiting weeks or months for a Termin at the Bürgeramt or a specialist doctor is normal, so 'endlich' gets a lot of use.

example_sentences.de: Vorher habe ich in Istanbul gewohnt.
example_sentences.en: Before that I lived in Istanbul.

cloze.en: We'll have a little something beforehand.

words.notes: 'vorher' is the adverb. For 'before' + a noun use the preposition 'vor': 'vor dem Essen'.

example_sentences.en: We can talk on the phone later.

cloze.de: Ich mache das ___, jetzt habe ich keine Zeit.
cloze.en: I'll do that later, right now I have no time.

words.notes: 'Bis nachher!' = see you later the same day. 'Bis später!' means the same.

example_sentences.en: Back then I was still a student.
Back then there was no internet.

cloze.de: ___ haben wir in einer kleinen Wohnung gewohnt.
cloze.en: Back then we lived in a small flat.

words.notes: Used for a clearly finished period in the past. 'früher' is the softer everyday alternative.

example_sentences.de: Neulich habe ich deinen Bruder getroffen.
example_sentences.en: The other day I met your brother.
I was at the doctor's recently.

cloze.en: The other day something strange happened to me.

words.notes: 'neulich' = one specific recent occasion. 'in letzter Zeit' = lately, over a period.

example_sentences.en: We'll be there in a moment.

cloze.en: The train is leaving in a moment.

words.notes: 'Bis gleich!' = see you in a minute. As an adjective 'gleich' means 'same': 'die gleiche Wohnung'.

example_sentences.en: The waiter is coming right away.

cloze.de: Bei einem Notfall musst du ___ 112 anrufen.
cloze.en: In an emergency you have to call 112 immediately.

words.notes: Stronger and more urgent than 'gleich'.
words.germany_context: 112 is the free emergency number for fire and ambulance anywhere in Germany; 110 reaches the police.

cloze.en: Excuse me, is this seat still free?

words.notes: 'hier' = at this place. For movement towards the speaker use 'hierher' or 'her'.
words.germany_context: 'Ist hier noch frei?' is the standard way to ask for a free seat in a full café, Biergarten or train.

example_sentences.en: I'll be there in a moment.

cloze.de: Der Paketbote war ___, aber ich war nicht zu Hause.
cloze.en: The delivery driver was there, but I wasn't at home.

words.notes: 'da' means both 'there' and 'present/available'. 'da sein' = to be there / to have arrived.
words.germany_context: If you are not 'da' when DHL rings, the parcel usually goes to a neighbour or a Packstation - check the yellow slip in your Briefkasten.

cloze.en: Please put the bag over there.

words.notes: 'dort' is more distant and a bit more formal than 'da'; in speech Germans usually just say 'da'.

example_sentences.de: Oben im Regal steht der Zucker.
example_sentences.en: The sugar is up on the shelf.

cloze.en: The neighbours upstairs are very loud.

words.notes: 'nach oben' = upwards. In lists 'oben' means 'above / at the top'.
words.germany_context: Ruhezeiten (quiet hours) are typically 22:00-06:00 plus all day Sunday - noise from the flat above is a classic reason for a polite note in the Hausflur.

example_sentences.de: Ich warte unten an der Tür.
example_sentences.en: I'll wait downstairs at the door.

cloze.en: The cellar is downstairs in the building.

words.notes: 'nach unten' = downwards.
words.germany_context: In most Mietshäuser the Briefkästen and the Keller are downstairs - your surname must be on the letterbox or post gets returned.

example_sentences.de: Gehen Sie an der Ampel links.
example_sentences.en: Turn left at the traffic light.
The supermarket is on the left.

cloze.de: Die zweite Tür ___ ist das Bad.
cloze.en: The second door on the left is the bathroom.

words.notes: 'links' = on the left, 'nach links' = to the left.

example_sentences.en: On the right you can see the station.

cloze.en: The exit is on the right.

words.notes: 'rechts' = on the right, 'nach rechts' = to the right.
words.germany_context: On escalators in German stations you stand on the right and leave the left free for people walking - ignoring it earns you glares.

example_sentences.de: Vorne im Bus ist noch Platz.
example_sentences.en: There is still room at the front of the bus.
I like sitting at the front.

cloze.en: The driver sits at the front.

words.notes: 'vorne' = position at the front, 'nach vorne' = towards the front. 'vorn' is the same word.

example_sentences.en: The toilets are at the back on the right.

example_sentences.de: Hinten im Zug ist es ruhiger.
example_sentences.en: It's quieter at the back of the train.

cloze.en: Please queue at the back.

words.notes: 'sich hinten anstellen' = to join the back of the queue.

cloze.en: It's raining, we'd rather stay inside.

words.notes: 'drinnen/draußen' describe position. For movement say 'rein' (in) and 'raus' (out).

cloze.de: Im Sommer sitzen alle ___ im Biergarten.
cloze.en: In summer everyone sits outside in the beer garden.

words.notes: Written with ß: draußen. 'im Freien' is the more formal version.
words.germany_context: The moment the sun appears, Germans move outdoors - Biergarten and café terraces fill up even at 12 degrees.

cloze.en: In Berlin there are building sites everywhere.

example_sentences.en: I can't find my key anywhere.
There was no free seat anywhere.

cloze.de: Am Sonntag findest du ___ einen offenen Supermarkt.
cloze.en: On Sunday you won't find an open supermarket anywhere.

words.notes: 'nirgends' means exactly the same and is a little shorter.
words.germany_context: Supermarkets close all day Sunday across Germany - only station shops, Tankstellen and Bäckereien sell food.

cloze.en: My card was suddenly gone.

words.notes: Adverb 'weg' (gone) has a short e; the noun 'der Weg' (path) has a long e. Different words.
words.germany_context: Bike theft is common in German cities - use a good lock and note your Rahmennummer, the police need it for a report.

example_sentences.de: Der Zug fährt um sechs zurück.
example_sentences.en: The train goes back at six.

cloze.en: I'll be back in five minutes.

words.notes: Also the separable prefix in zurückkommen, zurückgeben, zurückrufen.
words.germany_context: Online orders can be sent back within 14 days by law (Widerrufsrecht); returning goods in a shop is goodwill, not a right.

example_sentences.de: Fahren Sie geradeaus bis zur Kreuzung.
example_sentences.en: Drive straight ahead to the crossroads.

cloze.de: ___ und dann die erste Straße rechts.
cloze.en: Straight ahead and then the first street on the right.

words.notes: The classic answer to 'Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof?' - learn it together with links and rechts.

cloze.en: The rent is very high.

words.notes: 'sehr' goes with adjectives and verbs. Before a noun use 'viel': 'viel Geld', not 'sehr Geld'.

cloze.en: The coffee is quite okay.

words.notes: Before a strong adjective it means 'completely' (ganz kaputt); before a mild one it weakens to 'fairly' (ganz nett).

cloze.de: Der Weg zur Arbeit ist ___ weit.
cloze.en: The way to work is fairly far.

words.notes: Stronger than 'ganz', weaker than 'sehr'.

example_sentences.en: That is too expensive for me.

cloze.en: The coffee is still too hot.

words.notes: This 'zu' means 'excessively'. Don't mix it up with the preposition 'zu' (to) or the 'zu' in 'etwas zu essen'.

cloze.en: Did you sleep enough?

words.notes: 'genug' comes AFTER an adjective ('groß genug') but BEFORE a noun ('genug Zeit').

cloze.en: The bus was almost empty.

words.notes: Classic false friend: German 'fast' means 'almost', never 'schnell'.
words.mnemonic: German 'fast' is NOT fast - it means 'almost'.

cloze.en: There are hardly any free flats left.

words.notes: 'kaum' already contains the negation - never add 'nicht'.
words.germany_context: In big cities the Wohnungsmarkt is very tight: expect dozens of applicants per Besichtigung and have your documents ready.

cloze.de: Die Mieten sind in München ___ hoch.
cloze.en: Rents in Munich are especially high.

words.notes: 'nicht besonders' = 'not great' - a polite German way of saying something was bad.

cloze.en: I'm really sorry!

words.notes: On its own, 'Wirklich?' = 'Really?'. The casual spoken version is 'echt?'.

cloze.de: Im Kühlschrank ist nur noch ___ Milch.
cloze.en: There is only a little milk left in the fridge.

words.notes: 'wenig' with uncountables, 'wenige' with plural nouns. 'ein wenig' = a little bit.

cloze.de: In Berlin gibt es ___ zu sehen.
cloze.en: There is a lot to see in Berlin.

words.notes: Comparative 'mehr', superlative 'am meisten'. Before plural nouns use 'viele': 'viele Leute'.

cloze.en: I have no money left.

words.notes: Comparative of 'viel'. 'nicht mehr' / 'kein ... mehr' = not any more.

cloze.en: The flat is really expensive.

words.notes: Very common in casual speech, the relaxed version of 'wirklich'. As an adjective it means 'genuine, real'.

example_sentences.en: Aren't you coming? – Yes, I am!

cloze.en: Do sit down!

words.notes: Three jobs: (1) 'Doch!' answers YES to a negative question - 'ja' would be wrong. (2) In requests it softens: 'Frag doch mal.' (3) It marks surprise or a reminder: 'Du bist doch schon da!'
words.germany_context: 'doch' is the single most useful particle to learn - Germans use it constantly and English has no direct equivalent.

example_sentences.en: Could you help for a second?

example_sentences.de: Ich war schon mal in Köln.
example_sentences.en: I have been to Cologne once before.

cloze.en: Just wait a moment!

words.notes: Short for 'einmal'. It makes requests and commands sound friendly instead of bossy: 'Gib mir das' vs 'Gib mir das mal'.

example_sentences.de: Dann nehmen wir halt den Bus.
example_sentences.en: Then we'll just take the bus.

cloze.de: Ich habe keine Zeit, ich muss ___ arbeiten.
cloze.en: I have no time, I just have to work.

words.notes: Signals resignation: nothing can be done about it. More southern; northern Germans prefer 'eben'. Not the same as 'Halt!' = Stop!

example_sentences.de: Ich habe eben mit ihr gesprochen.

cloze.en: Then we'll just have to leave earlier.

words.notes: Three uses: 'Eben!' = exactly; 'eben' = a moment ago; and the northern equivalent of 'halt'.

example_sentences.de: Du weißt ja, wo ich wohne.
example_sentences.en: You know where I live, after all.

cloze.en: I did tell you that, you know.

words.notes: Unstressed 'ja' inside a sentence is NOT 'yes'. It means 'as we both know' or marks surprise, and it never takes a comma.

example_sentences.en: What are you doing here then?

cloze.en: Where is the toilet, then?

words.notes: In questions 'denn' makes you sound friendly and genuinely interested; without it questions can sound blunt. Don't confuse it with the conjunction 'denn' = because.

cloze.de: Der Chef kommt heute ___ nicht mehr.
cloze.en: The boss probably isn't coming in today.

words.notes: As a particle 'wohl' = probably / I assume. In 'sich wohl fühlen' it means 'comfortable, well'.

example_sentences.de: Eigentlich wollte ich zu Hause bleiben.
example_sentences.en: Actually I wanted to stay at home.

cloze.de: ___ ist der Laden am Sonntag zu.
cloze.en: Actually the shop is closed on Sunday.

words.notes: Two jobs: 'in fact / originally' (usually with a 'but' coming), and in questions a casual 'by the way'.

example_sentences.de: Wir essen und danach gehen wir spazieren.
example_sentences.en: We eat and after that we go for a walk.
After that I was very tired.

cloze.en: First the registration, after that the bank account.

words.notes: 'danach' points back to something already mentioned; 'nachher' just means 'later today'.
words.germany_context: Standard order after moving in: Anmeldung at the Bürgeramt within 14 days, then Bankkonto and Steuer-ID, then everything else.

example_sentences.de: Ich fahre meistens mit der Bahn.

example_sentences.en: I usually cook in the evening.

cloze.en: At the weekend I usually sleep in.
I would like a coffee, please.

words.notes: 'gern' + verb = to like doing something. Comparative 'lieber', superlative 'am liebsten'. 'gerne' is the same word.
words.germany_context: 'Ich hätte gern ...' is the polite standard for ordering at a Bäckerei, Imbiss or café - much better than 'Ich will'.

cloze.en: Of course you can park here.

words.notes: 'Klar!' is the casual spoken version, 'selbstverständlich' the formal one.

cloze.en: Maybe it will rain tomorrow.

words.notes: Watch the word order: when 'vielleicht' starts the sentence, the verb still comes second.

cloze.en: My brother lives in Berlin too.

words.notes: 'auch' stands directly before the word it emphasises, not at the end of the sentence like English 'too'.

cloze.de: Der Laden ist ___ bis 20 Uhr offen.
cloze.en: The shop is only open until 8 p.m.

words.notes: 'bloß' is the casual spoken alternative.
words.germany_context: Most supermarkets shut at 20:00 or 22:00 and all day Sunday - the big shop happens on Saturday.

example_sentences.en: The train is on time today.

cloze.en: Please be on time for the appointment.

words.notes: Opposite: 'unpünktlich'. 'rechtzeitig' means 'in good time' rather than 'exactly on time'.
words.germany_context: Punctuality is a genuine social rule: for a Termin, a job interview or a dinner invitation, arrive on the minute or five minutes early.

cloze.en: The flat is roughly 60 square metres.

words.notes: 'etwa' and 'circa' (ca.) are used the same way; 'ca.' is what you see in written adverts.

cloze.en: Hopefully I'll get the flat.

words.notes: One word replaces the whole English 'I hope that ...' - no extra clause needed.

example_sentences.en: I'll try it one more time.

cloze.en: Please explain that again.

words.notes: Spoken short form of 'noch einmal'. If you didn't catch something, 'Nochmal, bitte?' or 'Wie bitte?' both work.
